The cited line is a doc comment on the deliveryErrors interface field and is explicitly scoped to '(append/onDue)' failures, so it asserts the no-silent-drop property but does not carry the claim's headline ordering. That ordering is real elsewhere in the same file: append is awaited first under the 'durable accept FIRST' comment (:99-100) before the occurrence is pushed and onDue awaited (:107-111); an append failure records the error and continues so nothing is delivered (:101-106); a corrupt stream is skipped with a reported deliveryError (:87-92). Two bounds on the absolute wording: an unknown session (events === undefined) is skipped with no deliveryError at all (:83), and an occurrence whose onDue later fails is still counted in 'delivered' (:108 runs before :111).
verdicts.correction: Cite packages/schedule/src/driver.ts:98-117 for the accept-before-deliver mechanism; :35 is only the field's doc comment and should not be the sole evidence for an order guarantee.

packages/schedule/src/driver.ts:35 is a doc comment on the deliveryErrors interface field, and the file's own code bounds the 'never a silent drop' wording: an unknown session is skipped with no deliveryError (driver.ts:83), and an occurrence whose onDue throws is still counted in 'delivered' because driver.ts:108 runs before the await at :111.
